answer.evidence: The main body is a shelf unit drawn face-on. Its top is only a 2-row light board (rows 7-8) under decor goods and a sign (rows 1-6), which is a rim, not a top surface. Below it are three dark bays (rows 9-14, 16-21, 23-28) holding goods seen from the front. The shelf boards between them (rows 15, 22, 29) are 1-row light lines with no depth. No bay shows a receding top, an ellipse, or visible contents seen from above. The width is a constant 16 across all rows, so there is no side face. It reads as a front elevation, like the WRONG bookshelf reference.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small shelf endcap with a cream frame, a dark header band and shelves holding red, blue and yellow goods. It measures 22 visible tones per full 16x16 tile, above the stall (17) and hedge (9) and close to the well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no 5x5 flat fills. The 0% near-neutral share of dark edge pixels means the outline is tinted, a dark brown that follows the frame and goods, not a uniform black sticker line. The frame has about 4 lightness steps, slightly fewer than the references' 5-6. The goods and shelf edges carry per-item shading and small highlights, so texture is some, not rich. At the same scale it would sit next to the cheese stall without looking thinner or flatter.
